Really disappointed with my experience at Ortho Square.

Back in 2021, I got a dental implant done here along with bone grafting. At the time, I trusted them, but looking back now, I don’t feel the planning was done properly. There was no proper CT scan or detailed evaluation before starting, even though the implant area was close to the sinus.

During the procedure, they realised there wasn’t enough bone, so they went ahead with bone grafting and still placed the implant. From what I’ve now been told after scans, the implant wasn’t ideally positioned, and it eventually failed.

Fast forward to now (2026), I started having sinus problems. After seeing an ENT and getting a CT scan, it looks like there is foreign material in my sinus, likely related to that earlier procedure. I now have to go through endoscopic sinus surgery to fix it.

This has been stressful and honestly something that could have been avoided with better planning and care.

If you’re considering treatment here, please make sure proper scans are done and don’t hesitate to take a second opinion.

Why do teeth become shorter with age ?
When a patient says that their teeth are getting shorter then the first thing I notice is the teeth wear causing that is usually caused by teeth grinding either in daytime or while asleep. There is considerable amount of enamel loss that happens when teeth keep grinding with each other. Even the gastric reflux or acidity or ingestion of sour foods with acidic pH can dissolve enamel thus making it prone to chipping and fracture causing loss of teeth height.
Ageing of teeth can cause physiological wear and tear. This is not a disease. It is a sign of used teeth set for decades. There is another factor that makes teeth look shorter than before, is when your gums are swollen or rather abnormally inflamed thus giving a short teeth appearance.
Introspecting further into the signs, I ask for jaw pain or tightness of jaw when the patient wakes up or for teeth sensitivity to cold or hot drinks or if the teeth have discoloured yellow or if they look thin, to the patient. 
Most importantly, missing teeth can also lead to collapsed bite or faulty bite.

- Dr (Dr) Kruti N Dholakia
Beautiful Smiles. Inspiring Confidence.
